newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to speed sale of Balkan airlines.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to speed sale of Balkan airlines.

text.p: Bulgaria plans to select a consultant for the sale of the country's state-run Balkan Airlines by the end of July in a bid to speed up its privatisation, a senior official said on Thursday.

"By the end of July with the assistance of the (European Union's) Phare programme we hope to select an investment mediator and sign a contract," Alexander Sabotinov, executive director of the Privatisation Agency said.

"After selecting the consultant we plan to prepare new analysis of the company in the fastest possible way so that we will be able quickly to hold a marketing campaign, establish contacts and start negotiations with potential investors," he said.
Sabotinov said there had been already 14-15 firms which had shown interest to become Balkan's sale consultants "but it is more important how many will deposit offers".
Local media said on Thursday that Airbus was prepared to buy Balkan for one dollar and pay the company's debts.
Sabotinov admitted it had been "realistic" to sell the undebted airline for a symbolic sum taking into account the bad financial state of the airline. He said he had not studied an Airbus offer.
"Even a symbolic sum is something when a company suffers big losses," Sabotinov said after meeting foreign investors at a seminar in Sofia named 'Doing Business in Bulgaria'.
Officials decline to cite the size of Balkan's domestic and foreign debts.
Among the options for settling Balkan's foreign debts, suggested by the airline consultant KPMG, is consolidation of debts and an increase of the company's capital.

Balkan, which incurred losses of $50 million last year due to leasing fees, the drastic fall of the lev to the dollar and penalties on overdue payments, has returned all its four Airbus A320s leased from Japanese firm Orix Corp.
Two of the Airbuses were detained in London and Amsterdam for unpaid fees last December.
Bulgaria opened a procedure to privatise the national carrier in 1992 but in January 1995 the Privatisation Agency suspended it, citing a lack of potential buyers.
